library(flextable)
library(officer)
library(dplyr)


var_dict <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Domain,  ~Variable,                                      ~Baseline,        ~`Still Face`,     ~Reunion,          ~Total,
  "Infant", "Duration crying/negative vocal",                "blnegvoc",       "sfnegvoc",        "renegvoc",        "totnegvoc",
  "Infant", "Duration neutral vocal",                        "blneuvoc",       "sfneuvoc",        "reneuvoc",        "totneuvoc",
  "Infant", "Duration silent vocal",                         "blsilvoc",       "sfsilvoc",        "resilvoc",        "totsilvoc",
  "Infant", "Duration laughing/positive vocal",              "blposvoc",       "sfposvoc",        "reposvoc",        "totposvoc",
  "Infant", "Duration frown/negative expression",            "blnegexp",       "sfnegexp",        "renegexp",        "totnegexp",
  "Infant", "Duration neutral expression",                   "blneuexp",       "sfneuexp",        "reneuexp",        "totneuexp",
  "Infant", "Duration smile/positive expression",            "blposexp",       "sfposexp",        "reposexp",        "totposexp",
  "Infant", "Proportion of episode crying/negative vocal",   "blnegvocepi",    "sfnegvocepi",     "renegvocepi",     "totnegvocepi",
  "Infant", "Proportion of vocals that are negative",        "blnegvocprop",   "sfnegvocprop",    "renegvocprop",    "totnegvocprop"
)

prefix_colors <- c(bl = "#332288", sf = "#88CCEE", re = "#44AA99", tot = "#117733")
root1_words   <- c("neg","neu","sil","pos","yes","not","att","tlk","jnt","obj","par","comf","esc")
root1_color   <- "#882255"
root2_colors  <- c(lktch = "#88CCEE", look = "#CC6677", voc = "#CC6677", exp = "#CC6677",
                    tch = "#332288", atn = "#44AA99", aff = "#AA4499", end = "#CC6677")

match_first <- function(rest, candidates) {
  candidates <- candidates[order(-nchar(candidates))]
  for (cand in candidates) if (startsWith(rest, cand)) return(cand)
  NA_character_
}

segment_var <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || x %in% c("n/a", "")) return(data.frame(text = x, color = "black", bold = TRUE))
  prefix <- match_first(x, names(prefix_colors))
  rest   <- sub(paste0("^", prefix), "", x)
  root1  <- match_first(rest, root1_words)
  rest2  <- if (!is.na(root1)) sub(paste0("^", root1), "", rest) else rest
  root2  <- match_first(rest2, names(root2_colors))
  suffix <- if (!is.na(root2)) sub(paste0("^", root2), "", rest2) else rest2
  segs <- data.frame(text = prefix, color = prefix_colors[[prefix]], bold = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(root1)) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = root1, color = root1_color, bold = TRUE))
  if (!is.na(root2)) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = root2, color = root2_colors[[root2]], bold = TRUE))
  if (nzchar(suffix)) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = suffix, color = "black", bold = TRUE))
  segs
}

desc_word_patterns <- list(
  list(pattern = "negative",   color = root1_color,           bold = FALSE),
  list(pattern = "neutral",    color = root1_color,           bold = FALSE),
  list(pattern = "silent",     color = root1_color,           bold = FALSE),
  list(pattern = "positive",   color = root1_color,           bold = FALSE),
  list(pattern = "vocal",      color = root2_colors[["voc"]], bold = FALSE),
  list(pattern = "expression", color = root2_colors[["exp"]], bold = FALSE),
  list(pattern = "episode",    color = "black",               bold = TRUE)
)

segment_desc <- function(text) {
  matches <- list()
  for (p in desc_word_patterns) {
    locs <- gregexpr(p$pattern, text, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if (locs[1] == -1) next
    lens <- attr(locs, "match.length")
    for (k in seq_along(locs)) {
      matches[[length(matches) + 1]] <- list(start = locs[k], end = locs[k] + lens[k] - 1,
                                               color = p$color, bold = p$bold)
    }
  }
  if (length(matches) == 0) return(data.frame(text = text, color = "black", bold = FALSE))
  matches <- matches[order(sapply(matches, `[[`, "start"))]
  segs <- data.frame(text = character(0), color = character(0), bold = logical(0))
  cursor <- 1
  for (m in matches) {
    if (m$start > cursor) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = substr(text, cursor, m$start - 1), color = "black", bold = FALSE))
    segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = substr(text, m$start, m$end), color = m$color, bold = m$bold))
    cursor <- m$end + 1
  }
  if (cursor <= nchar(text)) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = substr(text, cursor, nchar(text)), color = "black", bold = FALSE))
  segs
}

apply_segments <- function(ft, i, j, segs) {
  chunks <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(segs)), function(k) {
    as_chunk(segs$text[k], props = fp_text(color = segs$color[k], bold = segs$bold[k]))
  })
  mk_par(ft, i = i, j = j, value = do.call(as_paragraph, chunks))   # mk_par, not compose — see below
}

ft_dictionary <- flextable(var_dict) %>%
  merge_v(j = "Domain") %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  set_table_properties(layout = "fixed") %>%
  width(j = "Domain", width = 0.6) %>%
  width(j = "Variable", width = 2.3) %>%
  width(j = c("Baseline","Still Face","Reunion","Total"), width = 1.1) %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Baseline",    color = prefix_colors[["bl"]],  part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Still Face",  color = prefix_colors[["sf"]],  part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Reunion",     color = prefix_colors[["re"]],  part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Total",       color = prefix_colors[["tot"]], part = "header")

var_cols <- c("Baseline", "Still Face", "Reunion", "Total")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(var_dict))) {
  ft_dictionary <- apply_segments(ft_dictionary, i, "Variable", segment_desc(var_dict$Variable[i]))
  for (col in var_cols) {
    ft_dictionary <- apply_segments(ft_dictionary, i, col, segment_var(var_dict[[col]][i]))
  }
}

  cursor <- 1
  for (m in matches) {
    if (m$start > cursor) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = substr(text, cursor, m$start - 1), color = "black", bold = FALSE))
    segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = substr(text, m$start, m$end), color = m$color, bold = m$bold))
    cursor <- m$end + 1
  }
  if (cursor <= nchar(text)) segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(text = substr(text, cursor, nchar(text)), color = "black", bold = FALSE))
  segs
}

apply_segments <- function(ft, i, j, segs) {
  chunks <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(segs)), function(k) {
    as_chunk(segs$text[k], props = fp_text(color = segs$color[k], bold = segs$bold[k]))
  })
  mk_par(ft, i = i, j = j, value = do.call(as_paragraph, chunks))   # mk_par, not compose — see below
}

ft_dictionary <- flextable(var_dict) %>%
  merge_v(j = "Domain") %>%
  theme_box() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  set_table_properties(layout = "fixed") %>%
  width(j = "Domain", width = 0.6) %>%
  width(j = "Variable", width = 2.3) %>%
  width(j = c("Baseline","Still Face","Reunion","Total"), width = 1.1) %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Baseline",    color = prefix_colors[["bl"]],  part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Still Face",  color = prefix_colors[["sf"]],  part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Reunion",     color = prefix_colors[["re"]],  part = "header") %>%
  color(j = "Total",       color = prefix_colors[["tot"]], part = "header")

var_cols <- c("Baseline", "Still Face", "Reunion", "Total")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(var_dict))) {
  ft_dictionary <- apply_segments(ft_dictionary, i, "Variable", segment_desc(var_dict$Variable[i]))
  for (col in var_cols) {
    ft_dictionary <- apply_segments(ft_dictionary, i, col, segment_var(var_dict[[col]][i]))
  }
}

title: Indicator, Predictor & ASP Profiles
text:
Overview
This page covers the descriptive class profiles from the 4-class latent profile analysis of Add Health Wave I adolescents (N = 6,469): the negative and positive risk-taking indicators that defined the classes, the demographic and parenting predictors tested as correlates of class membership, and the parenting-scale-level breakdown of the autonomy-supportive parenting (ASP) composite used throughout this project. The inferential odds-ratio work built on these profiles lives on the Odds Ratios page; effect-modification and BH-corrected robustness checks live on Interaction Effects & Comparisons.


Indicator Profiles

Overview
These panels show the 4-class latent profile solution’s indicator profiles from the negative and positive risk-taking indicators. Fit indices favored the four-profile solution: AIC/BIC improvements became marginal beyond four classes, the five-profile solution failed to replicate (a local maximum), and the four-profile solution showed adequate entropy (> .80) with theoretically coherent classes (LPA conducted in LatentGOLD; (Vermunt and Magidson 2005)).






PR = positive risk-taking; NR = negative risk-taking



The four profiles are:

C1 (High PR–Low NR, 35.6%)
C2 (Low PR–Low NR, 33.7%)
C3 (Low PR–High NR, 15.8%)
C4 (High PR–High NR, 14.9%)

Alcohol problems functioned as a near-binary separator: both C1 and C2 reported essentially no alcohol problems, while C3 and C4 reported substantially elevated problem counts. Within each of those two broad groupings, positive risk indicators (sports, school activities, friend disclosure, romantic involvement) were the primary source of further differentiation. However, adolescents with comparably low negative risk occupied meaningfully distinct profiles with respect to positive risk engagement (Duell and Steinberg 2019, 2021; Fryt and Szczygiel 2021).

Wrangle Profile Data
Binary indicators (probabilities, 0–1) and continuous indicators (means, 0–3) are plotted together on a shared primary axis. Continuous values are divided by scale_factor before plotting so they fit the 0–1 primary axis; the right-hand secondary axis reverses that transformation to show the true 0–3 scale.

# Legend labels with cluster size in parentheses
cluster_sizes <- c("C1" = 35.6, "C2" = 33.7, "C3" = 15.8, "C4" = 14.9)

cluster_labels <- c(
  "C1"      = paste0("C1 (", cluster_sizes["C1"], "%)"),
  "C2"      = paste0("C2 (", cluster_sizes["C2"], "%)"),
  "C3"      = paste0("C3 (", cluster_sizes["C3"], "%)"),
  "C4"      = paste0("C4 (", cluster_sizes["C4"], "%)"))

# Fill colors — no outlines
indicator_colors <- cluster_colors

# Scale factor: right axis max / left axis max (continuous max ~3, binary max 1)
# Continuous values are divided by this before plotting, then right axis
# multiplies back to show true scale. Edit here if any continuous value > 3.
scale_factor <- 3

# Label indicators
indicator_label_map <- c(
  WSDalc               = "Alcohol Problems",
  cigwhole             = "Cigarette",
  skipschool           = "Skipped school",
  liewhere             = "Lied about whereabouts",
  awayhome             = "Night out(unsanctioned)",
  dare_dum             = "Dangerous dare",
  seatbelt             = "No seatbelt",
  drvdrunk             = "Drove Drunk",
  BC_dum               = "Risky Sex",
  steal12M             = "Theft",
  phyfight             = "Fight",
  WSDsport             = "Sport Teams",
  WSDactivity          = "School Activities",
  avoidproblems        = "Problem Approach",
  disclose             = "Friend Disclosure",
  intitaterelationship = "Initiated Relationship")

# Continuous indicators — values can exceed 1 and read off the right axis
continuous_indicators <- c(
  "Problems from alcohol",
  "Sport Teams",
  "Extracurriculars",
  "Don't avoid problems")

# Negative panel: binary on left (0-1), continuous on right (0-3)
#   → continuous values divided by scale_factor to fit primary axis
# Positive panel: continuous on left (0-3), binary on right (0-1)
#   → binary values multiplied by scale_factor to fit primary axis
# This arrangement puts the 0-3 axes adjacent in the middle of the combined figure.

neg_continuous <- c("Alcohol Problems")
pos_continuous <- c("Sport Teams", "School Activities", "Problem Approach")

profile_long <- profile_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(Cluster1, Cluster2, Cluster3, Cluster4),
    names_to  = "cluster_raw",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cluster    = recode(cluster_raw,
                   "Cluster1" = "C1", "Cluster2" = "C2",
                   "Cluster3" = "C3", "Cluster4" = "C4"),
    cluster    = factor(cluster, levels = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4")),
    Indicators = factor(Indicators, levels = unique(Indicators)),
    # Rescale for plotting:
    #   Negative: continuous / scale_factor (plots on 0-1 axis, reads off right 0-3)
    #   Positive: binary * scale_factor     (plots on 0-3 axis, reads off right 0-1)
    value_plot = case_when(
      Risk == "Negative" & Indicators %in% neg_continuous ~ value / scale_factor,
      Risk == "Positive" & !Indicators %in% pos_continuous ~ value * scale_factor,
      TRUE ~ value ) )




BH Correction on Pairwise Comparisons
Non-estimable rows (p = “.”) and the Intercept block (included in LatentGOLD data export) are dropped before correction is applied across all remaining tests simultaneously.


code
pairs <- pairs_raw %>%
  filter(Indicator != "Intercept", `p-value` != ".") %>%
  mutate(
    p_value   = as.numeric(`p-value`),
    cluster_a = as.integer(clustera),
    cluster_b = as.integer(clusterb),
    Indicator = recode(Indicator, !!!indicator_label_map),
    pair      = paste0("C", cluster_a, " vs. C", cluster_b),
    p_adj     = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    sig       = p_adj < .05)


Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied here because every indicator is compared across all six class-pairs simultaneously; without correction, running this many pairwise tests inflates the false-positive rate well past .05 ((Benjamini and Hochberg 1995), (Benjamini and Hochberg 2000)). Overall, the negative risk indicators contributed about equally to differentiating classes, while positive risk indicators were the primary driver of separation within each alcohol-problem grouping.

code
# Builds axis labels as plotmath expressions so only the "M" renders in
# italics (the label text and parentheses stay plain). Named by the label
# text itself so ggplot matches each break by name — not position — which
# matters since p_neg/p_pos (and the line/z-score panels) each only show a
# subset of the full indicator list.
label_with_M <- function(labels_vec) {
  exprs <- lapply(labels_vec, function(lbl) {
    if (lbl %in% indicator_continuous_fig) {
      bquote(.(lbl) * " (" * italic(M) * ")")
    } else {
      bquote(.(lbl))
    }
  })
  out <- as.expression(exprs)
  names(out) <- labels_vec
  out
}

axis_labels_fig <- label_with_M(levels(factor(profile_long$Indicators)))

# make_panel() takes explicit axis config so Negative and Positive can differ.

# Negative: left = binary 0-1, right = continuous 0-3
#   primary axis shows 0-1; sec.axis multiplies by scale_factor to show 0-3

# Positive: left = continuous 0-3, right = binary 0-1
#   primary axis shows 0-3; sec.axis divides by scale_factor to show 0-1

# Create a function to make panel
make_panel <- function(risk_label,
                       left_name = "" ,left_lim, left_breaks,
                       sec_transform, right_name = "", right_breaks) {

  df <- profile_long %>% filter(Risk == risk_label)

  # Create panel
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Indicators, y = value_plot, fill = cluster)) +
     geom_vline(
  xintercept = seq(1.5, length(unique(df$Indicators)) - 0.5, by = 1),
  color      = "#DDDDDD",
  linewidth  = 0.4) +
    geom_col(
      position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width),
      width    = bar_width) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = indicator_colors, labels = cluster_labels,
                      name = NULL) + 
    scale_x_discrete(labels = axis_labels_fig) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = left_lim,
      breaks = left_breaks,
      labels = number_format(accuracy = 0.1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03)),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        transform = sec_transform,
        name      = right_name,
        breaks    = right_breaks,
        labels    = number_format(accuracy = 0.1)
     )
    ) +
    labs(title = paste(risk_label, "Risk Indicators"),
         y = NULL, 
         caption = str_wrap(
           "Note. Left y-axis (0\u20131) = binary indicators (probability of behavior).Right y-axis (0\u20133) = continuous indicators (within-class mean). Continuous bars are rescaled to the primary axis for display.", 
           width = 150)) +
    base_theme +
    theme(
      # adjust panel format from base theme
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 35, hjust = 1,size = axis_text_size),
      
      axis.title.y.right = element_text(
        size = axis_title_size, color = "gray40"),
      
      legend.position = "none",
      
      plot.caption = element_text(
                      hjust = 0,
                      lineheight = 1.2,
                      size   = 16),
      plot.title  = element_text(
        size = title_size, face = "bold",  hjust = 0.5))
      }

# Negative: left=binary(0-1), right=continuous(0-3)
p_neg <- make_panel(
  risk_label    = "Negative",
  #left_name     = "Probability (binary indicators)",
  left_lim      = c(0, 1.08),
  left_breaks   = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2),
  sec_transform = ~ . * scale_factor,
 # right_name    = "Within-class mean (continuous indicators)",
  right_breaks  = seq(0, scale_factor, by = 1))

# Positive: left=continuous(0-3), right=binary(0-1)
p_pos <- make_panel(
  risk_label    = "Positive",
 # left_name     = "Within-class mean (continuous indicators)",
  left_lim      = c(0, scale_factor * 1.08),
  left_breaks   = seq(0, scale_factor, by = 1),
  sec_transform = ~ . / scale_factor,
 # right_name    = "Probability (binary indicators)",
  right_breaks  = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2))

Sports participation, school activity involvement, and friend disclosure most clearly distinguish C1 (High PR–Low NR) and C4 (High PR–High NR) from C2 and C3, while alcohol problems and the broader negative-risk indicators most clearly separate the two alcohol-problem classes (C3, C4) from the two non-problem classes (C1, C2). The one indicator with limited discriminating power across all four classes was problem approach (class means ranged narrowly from 2.80–2.95, with only 4 of 6 pairwise comparisons significant).

Indicator Profiles - Standardized

Standardized Profile Panels
I also standardized based on the within class average for each indicator, allowing for a visualization of how each profile compares to the mean. The code used to create the figures is below.
Raw indicator profiles above mix binary probabilities and continuous means on different scales; z-scoring every indicator here puts all of them on the same standardized axis so their relative separation across classes can be compared directly, which the raw panels cannot show on their own.

Standardization
Class probabilities and indicator values are read in from the dissertation’s saved SPSS output (a 4-class LCA solution with an auxiliary ASP scale). Each indicator is then z-scored so the plotted classes are on a common scale.

# Variable names present in the indicator map
indicator_vars <- names(indicator_label_map)

# Standardize each indicator across the full sample
sav_scaled <- sav_raw %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(indicator_vars), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))

# Compute within-class means of z-scores
# Class variable assumed to be named "class" — update if different in your file
zscore_long <- sav_scaled %>%
  select(`clu#`, all_of(indicator_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(indicator_vars),
    names_to  = "variable",
    values_to = "z_score") %>%
  group_by(`clu#`, variable) %>%
  summarise(mean_z = mean(z_score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    cluster    = paste0("C", `clu#`),
    cluster    = factor(cluster, levels = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4")),
    label      = indicator_label_map[variable],
    Risk       = indicator_risk_panel[variable],
    label      = factor(label, levels = indicator_label_map[c(neg_order, pos_order)]) )

Z-Score Profile Panels
A horizontal reference line at z = 0 marks the sample average so it is immediately clear which profiles fall above vs. below the mean on each indicator.


code
# Function to create panel for profiles
make_zscore_panel <- function(risk_label) {

  # Set x-axis variable order
  panel_order <- if (risk_label == "Negative") {
    indicator_label_map[neg_order]
  } else {
    indicator_label_map[pos_order]
  }

  # Select columns from dataset
  panel_data <- zscore_long %>%
    filter(Risk == risk_label) %>%
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = panel_order))
  
  # Recode for graph 
  panel_data <- zscore_long %>%
    filter(Risk == risk_label) %>%
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = panel_order)) %>%
    mutate(mean_z = case_when(
      mean_z >  1.0 ~  1.1,
      mean_z < -0.5 ~ -0.6,
      TRUE          ~  mean_z))

  # Create plot
  ggplot(panel_data, aes(x = label, y = mean_z, fill = cluster)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "solid") +
   geom_vline(
    xintercept = seq(1.5, length(panel_order) - 0.5, by = 1),
    color      = "gray63",
    linewidth  = .8) +
    geom_col(

Older adolescents and adolescents with earlier pubertal timing were overrepresented in the two alcohol-problem classes (C3, C4), consistent with developmental increases in negative risk-taking across adolescence ((Duell et al. 2018), (Moffitt 2017)) and with the early-timing hypothesis linking earlier physical maturation to elevated risk propensity ((Natsuaki, Biehl, and Ge 2009)). Male adolescents were more likely to fall in the alcohol-problem classes, consistent with prior findings of higher delinquency rates among males (Miller, Malone, and Dodge 2010). Peer substance use was the single strongest and most consistent predictor, the only covariate with all pairwise comparisons against both C1 and C3 significant, matching developmental literature identifying peer behavior as a robust predictor of adolescent delinquency ((Thomas J. Dishion and Tipsord 2011; Thomas J. Dishion, McCord, and Poulin 1999; Henneberger, Mushonga, and Preston 2021)).

title: Odds Ratios: Predictors & ASP Scales
text:
This page tests whether the demographic, parenting, and peer predictors described on Profiles actually distinguish class membership, using posterior-probability-weighted multinomial logistic regression via the BCH three-step method to correctly account for measurement error in profile assignment (Bolck, Croon, and Hagenaars 2004), with all continuous predictors standardized prior to analysis.
In Section 2.1, Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied in R to the resulting pairwise comparisons (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, 2000). Running six pairwise cluster comparisons per predictor raises the odds that some comparisons look significant purely by chance, so Benjamini-Hochberg correction adjusts the p-values across that full set of comparisons and keeps the false discovery rate at an acceptable level before any pairwise difference gets flagged as significant.
In Section 3, predictor odds ratios (bar graphs and written summaries) are shown. Alternative line graphs of the odd ratios can be found in Section 4


code
# Shared by every OR section below to clean data import
tidy_params <- function(raw, cluster_cols) {
  raw %>%
    rename_with(~ "predictor_var", 1) %>%
    rename(omnibus_p = `p-value`) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = all_of(cluster_cols),
      names_to  = "cluster_raw",
      values_to = "log_odds") %>%
    mutate(
      predictor_label = recode(predictor_var, !!!pred_labels),
      log_odds        = as.numeric(log_odds),
      cluster         = recode(cluster_raw,
                          "Cluster1" = "C1", "Cluster2" = "C2",
                          "Cluster3" = "C3", "Cluster4" = "C4"),
      cluster         = factor(cluster, levels = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4")),
      OR              = exp(log_odds)) %>%
    select(predictor_label, predictor_var, cluster, log_odds, OR, omnibus_p)
}

text:
This page covers two robustness checks on the profile-membership findings from Odds Ratios:

whether the autonomy supportive parenting to profile association is moderated by biological sex or child age, and
a side-by-side view of BH-corrected indicator- and predictor-level comparisons

In Section 2, the ASP-predictor association is tested for moderation by sex and age. In Section 4, Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) corrected indicator- and predictor-level comparisons are shown side by side.

text:
BH Corrections
The indicator- and predictor-level patterns agree in direction: both sets of comparisons separate most sharply along the same alcohol-problem-status divide (C1/C2 vs. C3/C4) that structures the indicator profiles themselves, and peer substance use – the predictor with the most consistent indicator-level analog (negative risk indicators broadly) – is also the most consistently significant predictor. BH correction on top of the BCH-corrected estimates does not change this overall pattern; it affects which specific pairwise comparisons clear the FDR < .05 threshold; see Table 1 and Table 3 for the individual comparisons that did not.


code
# Clean, BH-correct, and relabel the indicator-level paired comparisons
pairs_6c <- pairs_raw %>%
  filter(Indicator != "Intercept", `p-value` != ".") %>%
  mutate(
    p_value   = as.numeric(`p-value`),
    clustera = as.integer(clustera),
    clusterb = as.integer(clusterb),
    pair      = paste0("C", clustera, " vs. C", clusterb),
    p_adj     = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    sig       = p_adj < .05,
    Indicator = recode(Indicator, !!!indicator_label_map))

# Clean, BH-correct, and relabel the predictor-level paired comparisons
pred_pairs <- pred_raw %>%
  filter(covariate != "Intercept", `p-value` != ".") %>%
  mutate(
    p_value   = as.numeric(`p-value`),
    class = as.integer(cluster_a),
    class = as.integer(cluster_b),
    pair      = paste0("C", cluster_a, " vs. C", cluster_b),
    p_adj     = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    sig       = p_adj < .05,
    covariate = recode(covariate, !!!pred_labels))

# Create function to do BH correction
apply_bh_cap <- function(raw) {
  raw %>%
    rename(predictor = Covariate, p_value = `p-value`) %>%
    filter(predictor != "Intercept") %>%
    mutate(
      p_value = as.numeric(p_value),
      p_adj   = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
      sig     = p_adj < .05 )
}

# Apply BH correction to the C1-reference paired comparisons

Neither interaction reached significance: ASP x sex, Wald = 1.45, p = .69; ASP x age, Wald = 4.32, p = .23. This means the ASP-profile association shown on the Odds Ratios page holds equally for males and females, and equally across the adolescent age range studied – higher ASP shifts profile membership toward C1 (High PR-Low NR) to the same degree regardless of the adolescent’s sex or age. This suggests parenting’s role in shaping risk-taking profiles is not confined to a particular developmental window within adolescence, nor does it operate through sex-differentiated pathways (Branje 2018).
